name: Managing Design-Phase Changes with ADU Design Contractors in LA

mainEntity.name: What are realistic design-phase change order scenarios with an ADU design contractor, and how can I minimize them in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: What are realistic design-phase change order scenarios with an ADU design contractor, and how can I minimize them in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Change orders are not just a construction issue; they also occur in the design phase and can quietly inflate soft costs. With ADU design contractors in Los Angeles County, common triggers include late decisions to add bedrooms or bathrooms, requests for custom rooflines or finishes, discoveries of easements or setbacks not previously considered, and additional requirements from plan-check reviewers or fire departments. To minimize these, invest in a thorough feasibility and programming phase: clearly define your must-haves versus nice-to-haves before your designer starts detailed drawings. Ask for a zoning and site constraint summary in writing so everyone understands setback, height, and coverage limits upfront. When you request changes, ask your designer to explain how they affect permitting complexity, engineering scope, and probable construction cost before proceeding. Build at least one structured review round into the process solely to catch alignment issues—budget, layout, and appearance—before the project moves into engineering. Finally, have your contract specify how design changes are billed and whether a new fee proposal is required for major scope shifts. This approach keeps design-phase change orders under control and helps you avoid a cascade of costly revisions.
acceptedAnswer.description: Design-phase change orders often arise from late layout changes, added custom features, new jurisdictional requirements, or unforeseen site constraints. Minimize them by finalizing your priorities early, insisting on a thorough feasibility study, and having your ADU design contractor flag cost or code impacts before revising plans.
